<!-- HOW THIS PAGE WORKS
     Each card below is one edition. To add a new edition, copy the top card,
     paste it above itself, and change the number, title, book, author, question,

     BOOK PHOTOS: upload a photo named edition-N.jpg (for example edition-5.jpg)

     Cards without a photo simply show no picture. -->

*The Marginalia* is a recurring literary essay series, published on LinkedIn, in which I revisit a book that has shaped my thinking. The name comes from my habit of writing in the margins of the books I read. Each edition is anchored by a passage that stopped me in my tracks and ends with a question for readers. Editions are listed newest first. Each card shows the closing question and links to the full essay on LinkedIn.

<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>What do you believe about people that you’ve never actually tested, only heard? And if you traced where those repetitions came from, how many would lead back to someone you’ve ever sat across a table from?</p>

<h3 class="card-title h5">Food, Cheer, and Song</h3>
<p class="card-text edition-book"><em>The Lord of the Rings</em><br>J.R.R. Tolkien</p>
<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>If the world really is full of dark places, who are the people who keep the light in view for you? And when was the last time you spent an evening with them over food, cheer, and song instead of more time with something you hoard?</p>

<h3 class="card-title h5">Each to Each, a Looking-Glass</h3>
<p class="card-text edition-book"><em>Human Nature and the Social Order</em><br>Charles Horton Cooley</p>
<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>Whose reflection of you do you trust most, and when did you last let that person hold your mirror? And to the people you pass today, online or off, what reflection are you providing back?</p>
<a class="btn btn-outline-primary btn-sm mt-auto align-self-start" href="https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/marginalia-edition-16-each-looking-glass-andrew-a-hanna-skh5c/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Read on LinkedIn</a>

<h3 class="card-title h5">The Purest Form of Generosity</h3>
<p class="card-text edition-book"><em>Reflections on the Right Use of School Studies</em><br>Simone Weil</p>
<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>Who gave you their attention at a moment in life that changed your direction, and do they even know it? Who in your life right now might be waiting for someone to listen about what they're going through?</p>

<h3 class="card-title h5">The Days That Must Happen</h3>
<p class="card-text edition-book"><em>Leaves of Grass</em><br>Walt Whitman</p>
<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>Who in your life has been iron to you; who cares enough to be hard on you? And when they are, do you hear it as a tribulation, or is it simply a reminder to you of the person they know you to be?</p>
<a class="btn btn-outline-primary btn-sm mt-auto align-self-start" href="https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/marginalia-edition-14-days-must-happen-andrew-a-hanna-i2ric/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Read on LinkedIn</a>

<p class="card-text edition-book"><em>Revisionist History</em><br>Malcolm Gladwell</p>
<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>What is the thing you most want to see change right now — and could the people you are asking to make a change tell, from the way you approach it, that you love it too?</p>
<a class="btn btn-outline-primary btn-sm mt-auto align-self-start" href="https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/marginalia-edition-13-respecting-what-we-trying-heal-andrew-a-hanna-5ff2c/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Read on LinkedIn</a>

<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>What ideas in your life are you not allowing yourself to sit with for longer than is simply efficient — and what might you get from the field that you're not getting from taking the shortcut across it?</p>

<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>What's the hardest thing that has happened to you — and if you're honest, what is telling the story currently getting you out of? If you set it down a while, not denied it, just set down for a while, what part of your life has been waiting offstage for you to notice that the theater might be empty?</p>

<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>What would it take for you to hear the word "ordinary" as a compliment instead of something lacking? And if it really is correct that reaching for extraordinary is what actually separates you from it, what, exactly, have you spent this year reaching for?</p>

<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>What's the "small stuff" you've had the hardest time convincing yourself is actually small — and has your relationship to it changed, or just your tolerance for carrying it?</p>

<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>Who advocated for you in a room you weren't in — and could you name them if you tried?</p>

<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>What's the belief you keep confirming on a technicality — accurate enough to survive every year, about the wrong thing entirely?</p>

<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>The next time the verdict arrives, wearing all its false confidence, what is the memory you could reach for that would let you laugh?</p>
<a class="btn btn-outline-primary btn-sm mt-auto align-self-start" href="https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/marginalia-edition-6-how-well-we-walk-andrew-a-hanna-wc4tc/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Read on LinkedIn</a>

<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>If you couldn't hand down the verdict from inside today — if you had to wait until you were far enough away to see the whole arc — how would you say your life is going, really? And whom would you trust to answer: the self living this one particular morning, or the one who has to remember all of them?</p>

<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>If we truly believed that we depended on other people's kindness, that we always have, and that one day soon, we will again, how differently would we move through the middle of our lives?</p>

<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>What question have you been avoiding by staying busy? And what might happen if you finally sat still long enough to hear the answer?</p>

<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>What's something you've been gripping too tightly? A title? A milestone? Some arbitrary metric? Perhaps they might actually arrive faster, or matter less, the moment you let go of it.</p>

<p class="card-text edition-q"><span class="edition-q-label">A question for your margins</span>Who is a friend you haven't spoken to in a while, but could call tomorrow and pick up as though no time had passed?
